title: Chapter 49: A Tale for the Future
content:
Chapter 49:

A Tale for the Future

—Subaru’s consciousness had been invited once again to the world drifting with black haze.

A world with nothing, ruled only by pitch-black “nothingness.”

With only his consciousness drifting in the void, Subaru vaguely recognized his own existence.

No one was there. There was nothing. Nothing happened.

No beginning. No end. A world where only inaction existed.

Surrendering himself to a vast, drifting sensation like being thrown into a night sea, Subaru’s consciousness abandoned even the act of thinking, sinking into the waves of nothingness.

Then, suddenly, a change occurred in that world of darkness.

Directly in front, someone stood before the eyes of Subaru, who was merely a consciousness.

A shadow stretched vertically from what seemed to be the ground, taking the form of a human and bringing its existence into relief.

Their face couldn’t be seen. Their figure was hazy. Yet, he vaguely thought it was the shadow of a woman.

The shadow wavered, slowly reaching a hand out toward him.

A distance where he could touch it if he just extended his fingers. And then, Subaru’s existence, which had been nothing but consciousness until then, realized he had gained fingers to respond to the fingers reaching out to him.

In a world that should have had nothing, a world where only consciousness drifted, a physical body reflecting that consciousness was born. Though, what manifested from here was only a right arm and a half-formed left hand.

His consciousness bewildered, he looked at the fingers extending before his eyes.

The fingers drew near with a gentle gesture, as if cherishing him, and for some reason, he felt an overwhelming urge to cry.

A mysterious sentiment, as if he had been longing to be treated so all this time.

The shadow writhed further, and as he impulsively tried to overlap his fingers with that hand—he stopped. No, he was stopped.

A white hand reaching from behind had enveloped Subaru’s extending hand.

A soft, almost hot sensation.

He wanted to turn around and see the owner of that palm. However, unlike his arm, his field of vision didn’t obey his will, and he absolutely couldn’t make the motion of turning around.

His movements were restrained as if forbidden, and gradually the strength of the touching palm grew stronger, pulling Subaru’s consciousness backward.

That meant parting with the shadow right in front of him.

The reaching fingers moved with agonising allure, as if pleading, as if clinging, beckoning to Subaru.

In contrast to his grasped right hand, he tried to touch those fingers with his free left hand, but the left hand that only existed halfway vainly clawed at the darkness, never reaching.

His heart trembled. Screaming his intense emotions. —But, a mouth to give them sound did not exist.

Drifting farther, drifting farther, fading away, the shadow.

It reached its fingers out one last time toward the near-crying Subaru,

“—ove you.”

That final word he couldn’t quite catch, even that grew hazy, and the world vanished.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

The first thing that entered the awakened Subaru’s vision was a familiar, luxurious ceiling.

In a mansion where aristocratic tastes were abundantly displayed, even a servant’s private room was in the realm of excessive decoration. When it came to a guest room meant to entertain visitors, the reality was that the design had to be excessive to show off the lord of the mansion’s authority and various other things.

Whatever the truth of that may be, for an average joe like Subaru, the discomfort was obvious.

Utilizing the shorter-than-average thought processing time it took to fully wake up, Subaru vaguely pondered such things.

And then,

“—Are you, awake?”

Exactly five seconds after opening his eyes, a voice called out to Subaru, whose consciousness was now completely awake.

The voice came from right beside the bed, from point-blank range at that. Tilting his head on the unusually soft pillow, Subaru looked over,

“…Guten Morgen, Rem.”

“Guu…? Is that a greeting from Subaru’s hometown?”

“Nah, by the standards here, it’s more like a regional dialect. Other than that, I only know ‘Danke’. ‘Buono’ is different, right.”

He suddenly felt anxious, wondering if this world had different languages depending on the country. Currently, since the exact mechanics of how Subaru’s verbal communication was functioning hadn’t been fully verified, he probably needed to handle issues around that quite carefully.

At any rate,

“Waking up with a maid right beside me, in a way, is a boy’s ultimate dream, isn’t it?”

“…Considering Rem’s blunder this time around, doing something like this as atonement is…”

“Ah, you sound like you’re about to go negative, so cut that out. Mo-re-im-por-tant-ly,”

Sitting up and shaking his head with every syllable, Subaru slipped his right hand out from under the covers. That hand was firmly intertwined with the blue-haired girl’s hand,

“Did I do this? Like, grabbed on and wouldn’t let go… If so, that’s pretty embarrassing. Like a kid refusing to let go of their favorite blanket.”

“No, um, this is, well…”

At Subaru’s question, Rem flusteredly moved her still-clasped hand, then, with her cheeks tinged just the slightest bit pink, she looked down,

“It was… from Rem.”

“What’s up with that? I’ll have you know, I might not look it, but I get terrible night sweats, you know? Especially around my hands and groin area. Heat rash in the summer is a literal matter of life and death.”

“Subaru was…”

“Yeah?”

Glancing repeatedly at their clasped hands, Rem mumbled evasively. Subaru, feeling calm, waited for her answer without rushing her.

Seeing Subaru’s patient posture, Rem took a few breaths, then looked up at him through her eyelashes,

“It looked like Subaru was suffering in his sleep, so… Rems hand…”

“You held it for me?”

“Rem is ignorant, talentless, and full of flaws. Therefore, she doesn’t know what she should do for someone at times like this. Because Rem doesn’t know, she thought she wanted to do the thing that made Rem the happiest when it was done for her.”

Perhaps because it connected to an embarrassing memory, her broken words were clumsy.

Even so, to Rem who had revealed her feelings to him, Subaru looked down at his still-held hand and let a faint smile touch his lips.

Subaru, who had been frightened like a child having a nightmare. Faced with him thus, this soft method was what she had chosen.

On a night when she, too, felt like crying, someone must have held her hand like this. The fact that she had done that for Subaru made him undescribably fuzzy and happy.

“That said, you’re sure putting yourself down an awful lot again, Rem-rin. That kind of thing isn’t good, you know. It’s easy to fall into a negative spiral, but it’s a real pain to get out of.”

“That might… be true. In Rem’s case, she has already lost sight of the exit.”

A feeble smile. He subtly didn’t like it.

While feeling something simmering deep in his heart, Subaru said,

“...Anyway, the follow-up, wait, no, I guess I want to hear how the whole thing turned out.”

“Yes. How much do you remember, Subaru?”

“Up to the point where Ros-chi descended with his energy maxed out while raining down fire, and an excited Rem-rin knocked me unconscious with a bear hug, I think.”

“…Then, about what happened after that.”

Hesitantly, Rem began to matter-of-factly relay the subsequent events.

After Subaru lost consciousness, Roswaal carried out a sweep of the ulgarms in the forest. Emitting the lingering scent of the Witch even while unconscious, he apparently functioned as live bait potent enough to erase the option of hiding for the witchbeasts lurking in the forest.

The pack that had been lost in the darkness of Shamak was wiped out by flames, and the remnants scattered throughout the forest were incinerated right along with them.

“So, about my curses for the time being…”

“Due to the death of the casters, there is no fear of activation. Master Roswaal, Lady Beatrice, and the Great Spirit have all already confirmed that the curses have lost their effect.”

“Well, if I’ve gotten up to a third opinion, I guess I’m safe…”

Since he couldn’t think of a specific area that was cursed, Subaru rubbed his chest area for the time being and let out a sigh of relief.

For now, the time bombs planted directly in his body had been defused. Remembering how many times he had nearly died to achieve that made it hard to breathe.

“Master Roswaal also directly subdued the chaos in the village. The children’s recovery is progressing well, and the village’s situation is mostly back to normal now.”

“I see, I see. But you know? Their beloved Subaru-niichan came back in a blood-soaked, battered state, so the brats must have been heartbroken. Were there even some who started crying? Ahhh geez, what can you do.”

“—Yes, that’s right.”

As she spoke, Rem slowly, suggestively peeled back Subaru’s blanket. He instinctively tried to curl up with an “Oh my~”, but immediately stopped that gesture.

The reason lay in Subaru’s clothes, which had been hidden by the blanket. It was the 

samue

-like outfit he had been dressed in on his first day at Roswaal Manor when he was brought in injured. However, there was an anomaly on the pants of that 

samue

. That was—

“Covered in scribbles… What is this, a cast for someone with a broken bone?!”

“By Master Roswaal’s courtesy, the children invited to the mansion left these writings behind.”

“Jeez, those brats…”

Stifling the urge to click his tongue, Subaru looked at the numerous scribbles written on him. From his perspective, they were upside down, and the handwriting was messy to begin with, making them incredibly difficult to read.

But because they were all written in the I-script that even Subaru could read, he was able to take his time and read through all of them.

“Jeez, those brats.”

The exact same words as before. However, the emotion layered into them was subtly different.

Using the bed’s pillow as a backrest, Subaru cast his gaze toward the window, wishing the time to go to the village would come as soon as possible.

“Thank you for bringing Rem-rin back.” “Thank you verrry much.” “You’re uncool, but you’re cool.” “Promise we’ll do ra-di-o calisthenics.” “Love you lots.”

“Hmph, idiots. It’s obvious 

I

 love you guys more!”

Saying ‘love’ so easily, your words are cheap

, Subaru thought.

Completely unaware that those exact thoughts would boomerang right back at him.

Subaru talked trash in a way likely to draw in a fondly exasperated stare. Seeing him like that, Rem suddenly corrected her expression, her lips trembling,

“Regarding your progress, this time Rem needs to talk about Subaru’s body.”

“Hm, ah, right. Setting curses aside, my body was actually in full-on crisis mode from other things too...”

As he spoke, he belatedly realized that the shoulder of the right hand being held by Rem was properly back in its socket.

Even applying a slight amount of force, there was no discomfort, nor did he feel any pain. It must’ve meant he had been treated, but the healing magic of this world truly was omnipotent.

Or so Subaru was thinking, but,

“Rem is sorry, Subaru.”

In front of the optimistically judging Subaru, Rem was bending at the waist, bowing her head.

Unable to think of a reason to be apologized to, Subaru waved his hand at her with a “Hey, hey,”

“Raise your head, Rem-rin. Physically I don’t feel bad at all, alright? My dislocated shoulder is back in, and my body parts don’t hurt anywhere in particular either. I’m in perfect shape, perfect shape.”

“That isn’t true. It’s true that the treatment for your visible wounds is finished, and fortunately, there’s no need to worry about any lingering aftereffects that would hinder your daily life. But—”

Cutting her words short, Rem cast a shadow of grief over her face,

“The scars will remain. On your body, of course, but also on your heart. Moreover, due to undergoing repeated treatments, the mana inside Subaru’s body is on the verge of exhaustion.”

“Ah, no wonder. I did think I felt a teensy bit sluggish… But that’s not really a big deal either. A man’s scars are medals, anywhere except on his back, and when it comes to emotional scars, I’m a pretty tough guy you know.”

Pointing a thumb at himself, Subaru showed a smile to try and erase her guilt.

It wasn’t a lie or anything. If Subaru’s heart were on a one-way track to being utterly weak and naive, he would never have been able to welcome a morning holding hands with her like this.

If they were going to talk about emotional scars, Subaru had been through experiences that would make it completely understandable if he could no longer look Rem directly in the face.

Thinking that far, Subaru stared intently at Rem.

Short blue hair. Her well-ordered features leaned more toward cute than beautiful. The expression he had initially thought showed little emotional variation now changed at a dizzying pace. She wasn’t scary. Not scary at all. There was the her who had sent Subaru into loops time and again, and there was the her who was now sincerely rejoicing at Subaru’s survival. He felt that it was all simply a matter of fate and circumstances.

Just as there was a Rem who ran wild out of concern for Roswaal, there was also a Rem who jumped to hasty conclusions out of concern for Subaru, and it was also a fact that there was a Rem who would enter a reason-flung-aside berserker mode once she concluded there was no worry of friendly fire—.

“You seem calm, but Rem-rin, you’re actually not cool and collected at all, are you?”

Her usual attitude at the mansion, and her work ethic as the senior maid instructing Subaru. When considering those as a baseline, Rem seemed like an exceptionally capable individual with calm judgment.

But when a situation deviated from that domain, he couldn’t help but feel she possessed a nature that made her instantly start rushing off in completely absurd directions.

Subaru was in no position to criticize others for a tendency to make snap judgments, but in her case, it was accompanied by the use of force—and the actual capability to use that force—which made it troublesome.

At Subaru’s pointing this out, Rem froze for just an instant, then weakly looked down.

With her face cast down like that, she muttered,

“Rem… is aware.”

Muttering, she continued, as if spilling the feelings in her heart piece by piece.

“Rem is powerless, talentless, a dropout of the Oni clan. So no matter what, even if she started running, there are many things she can’t reach. Therefore, in order for Rem to catch up to Sister, she can’t think of any other method than starting to run early.”

Covering her face with her free hand, Rem continued her confession as if squeezing it out.

“Sister could have done it better. Sister wouldn’t have stumbled in a place like this. Sister surely wouldn’t have hesitated. Sister would have handled it easily, without a doubt. Sister absolutely wouldn’t have made a mistake. If it were Sister, if it were Sister, 

if it were Sister

—”

Cutting her words, Rem looked at Subaru with a frail light dwelling in her eyes.

What welled up in her eyes were not tears. It was pure emptiness—a despair steeped in resignation.

“Rem is… a substitute for Sister. And an incredibly, incredibly inferior one at that—a defective product who will never be able to catch up to the real Sister, no matter how much time passes.”

—Suddenly, droplets faintly welled in her eyes.

“Why, was the horn left on Rem? Why, wasn’t Sister’s horn the one that remained? Why, was Sister born with only one horn? Why—were Sister and Rem twins?”

As if searching for her reason to exist, Rem’s lips trembled.

The drops welling in her eyes rolled down her cheeks, leaving a sorrowful glisten on her white skin.

Subaru fell silent. As if unable to bear that silence, Rem hastily wiped her tears and, her expression crumbling into a terribly forced smile,

“R-Rem is sorry. She said something strange. Please forget it. This is the first time she has ever talked about something like this with another person, so things got weird…”

“Hey, Rem.”

Spoke rapidly, trying to completely erase her previous remarks.

Interrupting her words, Subaru called her name. Breaking the silence, what kind of words would he form? Rem looked up, as if terrified of the answer.

To her, Subaru said,

“Where’s the punchline?”

“—Huh?”

“I’m saaaaying, the punchline. The punchline. That moment that suddenly sweeps the living room into roaring laughter. There’s gotta be something, right, after talking that much?”

Not understanding what Subaru was saying, Rem darted her eyes in confusion,

“What on earth are you…”

“Your talk was 

that

 devoid of comedic value, is what I'm saying. —Rem, this is the continuation of our interrupted conversation. Remember?”

At his question, Rem’s eyes clouded over. Seeing her reaction, Subaru laughed with a “Can’t be helped, huh,” raised his left hand, and held up one finger right in front of Rem’s eyes.

“Alright then, let’s review. First point of idiocy. You saying you couldn’t save me. Can you see me alive and kicking right in front of you? I’ve even got my feet firmly attached.”

He punctuated it with action by loosely swinging his legs. Rem seemed to realize the context of what Subaru was bringing up, but she still weakly shook her head,

“That’s just hindsight…”

“People in the old days said ‘all’s well that ends well.’ If we graded things along the way, to be honest, I’d be way more unwatchable than you. Putting that aside, the second point of idiocy. Trying to shoulder everything and do it all by your lonesome, got it?”

Winking, Subaru held up a second finger,

“Well, running wild for my sake makes me happy, I suppose, but that also depends on the time and place. Above all, if you just talk things through, a good idea’s bound to come up, right?”

Regarding the witchbeast hunt, it was self-evident that Subaru’s words held a point. Rem’s lips trembled as if ashamed of her own short-sightedness, swallowing any words of rebuttal back down her throat.

However, this was exactly the kind of hindsight bias one could only preach after seeing the result—Rem, overwhelmed as she was, didn’t notice this, and Subaru secretly stuck his tongue out, apologizing for being mean.

Then, Subaru slid his face under hers as she looked down.

He smiled at her as she was startled, held up his third finger on his left hand, and said,

“And with that, the third point of idiocy I didn’t get to say. No, the third one kind of slipped out quietly back then, so accurately, this is the fourth point of idiocy. Just riddled with idiocy.”

“Because Rem did things that leave her no choice but to be told that.”

“Yep, that right there. That’s the fourth point of idiocy.”

Pointing his finger at Rem, who couldn’t break out of her self-deprecating loop, Subaru made the callout. Then, fluttering four raised fingers, he said,

“Worrying about things that are in the past forever and only ever looking backwards.”

“—”

“You know, Rem, you keep saying ‘if it were Sister, if it were Sister,’ putting Ram on a pedestal to death while tearing yourself down… but I don’t think having Ram-chi in Rem-rin’s position would’ve made the situation any more positive, you know? She has less stamina than Rem-rin, she’s a bad cook, she slacks off at work, she’s got a foul mouth… maybe just a tiny bit more thoughtful, I guess?”

Recalling Ram’s specs, Subaru thought about the sheer divergence between her and the ideal image Rem spoke of. An older sister who was inferior to her younger sister in every ability. Just as they themselves were aware, Ram was inferior to Rem in every stat. To the point where there was absolutely no need for Rem to put herself down at all.

At Subaru’s impression, however, Rem shook her head in rejection,

“N-No, that’s not it. Sister is, the real Sister is much different. If she had her horn, if Sister had her horn, things like this…”

“But Ram doesn’t have that ‘if she had’ horn. So, I don’t know a single thing about this high-spec Ram with a horn.”

Cutting off Rem, who tried to deny herself with predetermined answers, Subaru touched his chin with his left hand,

“The Ram I know is exactly as I just said. She’s worse at cooking, sewing, cleaning, etiquette, and talking than Rem. —Well, I think that’s the good part about her, though.”

Her way of speaking was so utterly arrogant that bumping heads once in a while wasn’t bad.

That kind of distance in his relationship with her was comfortable for Subaru. And if he turned the issue toward the presence or absence of a horn,

“Probably, the only one worrying about that is you, Rem.”

He recalled his brief conversation with Ram in the forest.

It seemed to him that Ram hadn’t retained much attachment to being an Oni. On the contrary, it felt like she wanted to do something to resolve Rem’s obsession with it.

Subaru never arrogantly thought about fixing that for her.

In the end, he was nothing more than a youngster whose life experience was shallow beyond belief, a shut-in whose life density was far thinner than others his age.

How could the lip-service preaching of a guy like that resonate with anyone’s heart?

He didn’t get worked up. He didn’t even try to make it resonate.

Because things one must come to terms with inside themselves can ultimately only be managed by oneself, not by clinging to someone else.

Therefore, what Subaru told Rem was a terribly simple imposition of his own feelings.

“If you weren’t there, I’d definitely be dog food and dead by now. I was saved thanks to you being there. I’m alive like this now. Not just thanks to Sister, but thanks to you.”

“…If it were the real Sister, she would have done it much better.”

“Maybe so. —But, the one who was there for me was you.”

Overwriting her weak rebuttal, Subaru placed his left hand over his still-clasped right hand.

To Rem, who gasped and looked up, Subaru showed a wry smile,

“I’m glad you were there, Rem. Thank you.”

“—!”

At the words Subaru spoke, Rem let out a groan that sounded like her throat was seizing.

Then she turned her face away, keeping her expression hidden from Subaru,

“Rem is… She has always been nothing but a substitute for Sister…”

“Quit it with that sad self-definition. To begin with, you and Ram are different right down to your categories. I mean, older sister attribute versus younger sister attribute—depending on the situation, wars break out over that.”

A difference in tastes that could never be reconciled. Both have their own good points, Subaru thought internally, while Rem squeezed her eyes tightly shut.

“Well, you know. Make a bit more use of the advantages of being twins from now on. Since Ram’s quick-thinking mind is held back by her physical body, Rem can just handle the parts she can’t keep up with. Covering for each other’s flaws with beautiful sisterly love, that makes you the strongest.”

“As she thought, Rem’s short-sightedness is a flaw, isn’t it…”

“We’re in a good flow right now, so don’t nitpick there. Oh, right. I just thought of something.”

Clapping his hands, Subaru’s face lit up as if struck by a brilliant idea.

Then, leaning closer toward Rem, who was still turning her face away,

“Earlier, you asked, right, Rem-rin? Things like why Ram doesn’t have a horn, and you do.”

“…Yes.”

“Well, I haven’t asked deeply about the reason she lost her horn, and I’m not gonna ask, so I don’t know. And speaking as if I understand precisely because I don’t know, you see.”

Subaru tapped the top of his own forehead with his left hand—right around where Rem’s horn had sprouted,

“Rem, you can just act as the substitute for the horn that Ram doesn’t have. The two of you can get along and play the role of the ‘Oni’ together. Gives it a heartwarming feel.”

“—Ah.”

“Besides, you say you’re a substitute, but Ram truly has no substitute for you, Rem, you know? Can you even imagine the state Ram would be in if you were to disappear?”

A speechless Rem didn’t know, but Subaru knew the future where that had happened.

The figure of her, screaming at her sister’s death, shedding grief-stricken wails as if the world had ended, and going mad as she tried to avenge her with every ounce of power she possessed.

“…But.”

Even so, Rem still wouldn’t smoothly nod at Subaru’s words.

Anyway, convincing people was hard. In her case, she had probably been struggling to handle those emotions for many long years, so the lump in her heart calcified, its hardness ironclad.

To such an unyielding girl, Subaru scratched his head with an “Ah, geez,”

“Alright, then let’s do this. Rem, you compare yourself to the ideal Ram in your head, and no matter how you struggle, you feel like you’re stuck in a rut. In that case, just erase that idol of an ideal Ram you keep comparing yourself to.”

“Rem can’t do something like that so easily. Rem has always… with Sister…”

“So if you want an evaluation, ask me. I’ll hand you a realistic one myself, way more so than the Ram in your head. Let me tell you, I have zero ability to read the room, so I’m gonna be blunt. No flattery, no mercy, none of that stuff at all. Serves you right.”

Smiling at her, Subaru mussed up Rem’s blue hair with his left hand.

To her, who narrowed her eyes as if it tickled, Subaru let out a small sigh,

“In my hometown, we have a saying: ‘If you talk about next year, the demons will laugh.’ So, you see.”

To Rem, who couldn’t say anything and just let him do as he pleased, Subaru tilted his head and continued his words.

“Laugh, Rem. Don’t look so glum, laugh. While laughing, let’s talk about the future. For all the wasteful time you’ve spent looking backwards until now, from now on, let’s talk while looking forward. To start with, we can even just talk about tomorrow.”

“…About, tomorrow.”

“Yeah, about tomorrow. Anything’s fine, you know? Like, whether tomorrow’s breakfast menu should be Japanese or Western-style, or whether to put your socks on starting with the right foot or the left—something silly like that is fine. No matter how boring it is, we can talk about tomorrow because tomorrow exists.”

Spreading his hands, Subaru wrapped up his speech like that, and shrugging his shoulders with a “How about it?”, he asked Rem for an answer.

She hesitated to reply for a moment, then lowered her eyebrows as if troubled,

“Rem is very weak. Therefore, she will surely end up leaning on you.”

“Isn’t that fine? I’m also weak, and stupid, and have a bad look in my eyes, and can’t read the room—just saying it myself makes me depressed, but I live relying on others and expecting the people around me to cover those areas. We can just lean on each other as we move forward.”

Because you take on absolutely everything yourself, you only end up looking at that heavy burden, and lose sight of the path ahead of you.

If you walked around intending to keep both hands completely empty like Subaru, you’d have it easy. Even then, baggage would naturally pile up before you knew it—but if carrying it alone means you cannot see ahead, all you have to do is share the load with someone as you move forward. Something like that, how about it?

“Let’s put our arms around each other’s shoulders while laughing, and talk about the future called tomorrow. You know, talking about next year while laughing with a Demon has always been a dream of mine.”

“…That’s quite demonically possessed of you.”

“Right?”

When he closed one eye and skewed the corner of his mouth, Rem also let out a small laugh, as if drawn in.

She started to laugh, and from the corners of her laughing eyes, tears suddenly spilled out. In large drops, the tears that knew no end flowed and flowed exactly as they welled up, and yet Rem continued to laugh.

Laughing and crying, crying and laughing, Rem pressed her face into the blanket as if to stifle her sobs and laughter, yet her tearful laughter still fell quietly into the room.

Subaru gently continued to stroke her hair the entire time.

His right hand remaining firmly clasped, all the way until the very end.

Forever gently, gently, continuing to stroke it.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

He cast his mind back over his days at Roswaal Manor.

The first loop began, and he died on the night of the fourth day—cause of death: debilitation.

Entering the second loop, he died on the night of the fourth day—cause of death: beaten to death by Rem.

Despairing in the third loop, he died on the evening of the third day—cause of death: brutally murdered by Ram.

Rousing himself in the fourth loop, he died on the evening of the fifth day—cause of death: throwing himself off a cliff.

And then, the fifth loop. He got completely chewed up by dogs here and there, violently gouged by claws here and there, lost a massive amount of blood and mental stamina, and was left with scars all over his body that made him want to avert his eyes—but he felt he had managed to scoop up everything.

His relationships with Rem and Ram, Subaru’s standing within the mansion. He saved the village children, and the witchbeasts in the forest had been purged, eliminating the danger. This adventure spanning roughly twenty days was a complete triumph.

Yes, it was supposed to be a complete triumph.

“—It’s not like I’m angry. Yes, exactly, I’m not angry at all. Just because the person I was desperately nursing wasn’t there when I woke up, and when I thought about going to look for him I was tied up tight to a chair, and I was completely left behind—I am not someone so small-minded that I’d get angry over something like that.”

…If not for the presence of the girl sitting in the chair beside his bed, twirling her silver hair with her fingers, backing Subaru into a corner in a foul mood like that.

Sweating buckets of cold sweat, Subaru silently listened to her resentful complaints.

Ten minutes had already passed since she visited his room, but the majority of that time had been dominated by these grievances wearing the guise of a lecture.

Though, it conveyed her earnestness that when she first entered the room, she thoroughly worried about the condition of Subaru’s body, let out a sigh of relief after confirming there were no issues, and only then sat in the chair as if composing herself, shifting gears before she started.

Be that as it may,

“I’m really, not, angry, you see.”

“Yes, Emilia-tan’s anger is completely justified. Yes, I’m sorry.”

“I keep telling you I’m not angry, gosh. But, if Subaru thinks he’s at fault, then it can’t be helped. I shall accept that apology. —Really, don’t make me worry so much.”

Subaru apologized, swallowed up by Emilia’s momentum. To him being like that, Emilia smiled as if getting her way, and then finally, adding a tinge of affection to her smile, she added that last part.

That was super unfair. Being told something like that with a face like that, how could he possibly brush it off?

After Rem had cried her heart out and taken her leave from the room (at which time she strongly emphasized, “The fact that I cried is an absolute secret,” so he was currently pondering how to spread it around without her finding out), Emilia was the one who visited Subaru while he was dozing off.

Her actions since visiting were as previously described. However, after all of that had run its course, what welled up in her eyes was purely a compassionate light anxious for Subaru’s well-being, and that couldn’t help but leave him warmly flustered.

“Even so, you really are a boy with no end to your injuries, Subaru. The reason you even came to this mansion was because you were injured… and it’s only been four days since then.”

“It’s not like I’m getting injured because I enjoy it, you know? It’s just purely that the world is built to be a little harsh on me, or maybe... at least, Emilia-tan, it’d be totally okay if you just unconditionally spoil me to balance it out!”

“Even though you ran away when I tried to be sweet to you. I don’t care anymore.”

“Gwaaaah! I threw away the chance myself! Damn it, Beako, you could’ve done a slightly better job! What the heck is tying her up tight?!”

Screaming the name of the drill-haired girl whose face he hadn’t seen since waking up, Subaru took his unreasonableness out on her.

At the word ‘tied up tight’ that Subaru spoke, Emilia stared off into the distance,

“I fell asleep while sitting in the chair, and when I woke up, I was secured to the backrest. I was absolutely flabbergasted.”

“Who even says flabbergasted these days…”

“Don’t make fun… Puck was also trying his hardest to stop me from chasing after you guys, and what would have happened if Roswaal hadn’t returned? Do you understand?”

Pouting her lips, Emilia looked slightly angry.

At her words, Subaru had no choice but to respond with utmost humility.

Just as Puck had intended, he had maneuvered to keep Emilia out of danger, and Beatrice had apparently quickly given up on the method of successfully persuading her, shifting instead to forcibly sealing her actions.

Having her path blocked by the two of them and being left completely helpless, he could imagine her state of mind must have been quite miserable.

If he had been the one left behind, he couldn’t help but feel the same way.

Although, he could confidently say that even if the exact same thing happened again, Subaru still wouldn’t bring her along.

“But, I ended up being saved by you again, didn’t I.”

“Huh?”

“I said, I ended up being saved by you again. Even though we invited you to the mansion to thank you for saving my life, here you go again. Thank you, soooo much.”

Overlapping her hands, Emilia broke into a helpless smile and told him.

Receiving that, Subaru finally replied with an “Ah,”

“Nah, it’s fine, it’s fine. It’s just something I did because I wanted to, and it’s not like it was unrelated to me. Yeah. I… actually did it, didn’t I.”

As he spoke, he was finally able to grasp the reality of it.

He felt as if the hardened knot inside his chest dropped with a thud.

The repeated days of roughly twenty days he looked back on—Subaru had seen their endpoint.

After having his heart chipped away, broken, and crushed that much, the thing he still sought after despite it all had finally, finally come to a place within his reach.

He was finally able to feel it for himself, that he had accomplished it.

“I thought you would say that, but that won’t satisfy me. Even Roswaal, and surely Ram and Rem too, will want to thank you, Subaru.”

“Is that so… Then, I’ll take you up on that offer. I’ll have Ros-chi revise my employment conditions into something even better, and Ram and Rem will be my personal maids for a while, mufufu. A-N-D!”

Laughing lecherously with a hand over his mouth, Subaru swayed his body side to side and leaned toward Emilia, pointing a finger at her as she drew back slightly,

“Is Emilia-tan the type to give me a reward too?”

“…You’re so calculating. I’ll have you know, it’s only if it’s something I can actually do. …When I said that before, you asked for my name, didn’t you.”

“Heheh, don’t underestimate my greed. This time around, I've got nothing to do with such softness. Avarice, greed, a swirling libido drives me!”

Even though he couldn’t stand up from the bed, Subaru struck a wild pose, raising both arms diagonally.

Seeing him in such high spirits, she likely didn’t think an anticlimactic request was coming; Emilia straightened her posture and turned to face him properly.

At Emilia’s attitude that practically said ‘Let’s hear your request,’ Subaru nodded, then quickly searched through the ‘Emilia Reward List’ he desired in his brain.

Amidst the expanding set of options, from a little adventure to flashily skipping steps on the relationship staircase, Subaru sifted through and pondered them deeply before choosing one.

And then,

“Then, go on a date with me, Emilia-tan.”

With that, he decided to make the promise he had made twenty days ago with her once again.

“A deit?”

“It means going out together, just the two of us, seeing the same things, eating the same things, doing the same things, and sharing the same memories.”

“…Are you okay with just that?”

“Just that, is exactly what I want.”

The very first step had started from there.

How many hardships had Subaru piled up just to have that long-desired date with her.

Along the way, various feelings had piled up, and the hurdles Subaru sought through his loops continued to constantly rise, but the final hurdle he wished to jump over was always right there.

Therefore, to conclude these repeating days, that promise was the most fitting.

“I wanna brag about Emilia-tan to the village brats, and there are some amazing flower fields. Even just walking around aimlessly is special to me.”

“The meaning of greed in your head might be different from the norm, you know?”

“Keep saying that. Soon enough, even that smile will freeze over at my audacity. Yes!”

Crossing his arms in a mysterious pose.

Watching Subaru unable to hide his soaring emotions, Emilia floated a smile that looked entirely drained of tension,

“Okaaay, understood. I will go on a deit with you, Subaru.”

“Hell yeah! That’s what I’m talking about! E-M-B! (Emilia-tan, Maji, Bosatsu!)”

The promise made, Subaru pumped his fist and loudly declared that.

Listening to Emilia’s small sigh, he looked out the window with an elated feeling, eagerly awaiting his body’s recovery.

The direction of the village, the promised destination of their date.

While letting his thoughts run to that, Subaru suddenly thought of the witchbeast forest.

The curses dwelling within Subaru’s body—he was told they had all lost their effect.

That meant the sweeping of the ulgarms in that forest. The details of this incident, which started from a single one slipping through the gap in the broken barrier and entering this side.

In the end, it meant that everything had been settled in the form of the annihilation of one side.

There was an incomprehensible bad aftertaste.

He wasn’t in a mood where he could simply rejoice unconditionally that the harmful beasts were gone.

Suddenly, he remembered.

The sensation of thrusting his sword into the body of that witchbeast, completely lost in the moment within the forest.

The sensation of driving steel into flesh was distinct, and the feeling remaining in his palms was still fresh in his memory.

That sensation, of taking a life.

He figured that even a sensation like that would probably be forgotten someday.

He figured that with the passage of time, this incomprehensible feeling currently coming and going in his chest would surely fade away.

A sensation he hadn’t known until he came to another world.

Until the day came when he’d forget it, what could he do—

“Subaru.”

“Yeah?”

Called out to, he turned around.

Subaru’s gaze, which had been vague and distant—how had she interpreted its meaning?

Emilia brushed up her silver hair, walked over to the window, and opened the curtains.

The obstructed sunlight flooded into the room all at once, and her silver hair was swallowed up by the dancing light, gently pulling Subaru’s eyes into that scene.

And, to the silenced Subaru, Emilia offered a soft smile,

“On the day of our deit, let’s bring a bouquet of flowers.”

“—Yeah.”

Receiving that smile, Subaru covered his face with his hand, thinking he was no match for her.

Until the day came when he’d eventually forget, he intended to engrave it in his heart so he doesn’t forget.

It was hypocrisy, and an intrusive sentiment, but he believed it wasn't wrong.

Because he felt as if Emilia’s smile had told him it was right.

Just the two of them, Subaru and Emilia, time passed as they smiled at each other.

—The morning sun of the fifth day, which had finally arrived, continued to illuminate the two of them gently.
